messages:
emily_support: heads-up — support ticket #C-4892. Customer (big-ecom) reports intermittent 503/500 from hosted inference API starting ~08:12 UTC. They see a large spike in failed calls and some trace ids: trace=tr-9a1b2c3d. Occurs on their high-throughput endpoint using the text-generation route. Can SRE/runtime take a look? @jordan_sre @alex.connor :eyes:

jordan_sre: looking. quick question — are these 503s all coming from the same region/zone? I can already see an increase in upstream restarts in the monitoring (pod restart spike). Pinging logs now. :mag:

alex.connor: grabbing the worker logs for the timeframe. Preliminary snippet from /var/log/worker/inference-2026-03-15.log around 08:12:

```
2026-03-15T08:12:34Z [err] model-serving: runtime exception: CUDA out of memory while allocating 512MB
2026-03-15T08:12:34Z [crit] inference_worker[pid=12453]: terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
2026-03-15T08:12:34Z [err] inference_worker[pid=12453]: signal 6 (SIGABRT), fault address 0x0
2026-03-15T08:12:36Z [info] kubelet: Killing container with id docker://inference-worker: exit code 137
```

This looks like OOM followed by the container being killed. :fire_engine:

emily_support: customer says failures started after a model bump yesterday (we pushed v2.3.8 with a perf change). They report billing/throughput impact and want ETA. Maria from CS is on the thread. @maria_pm

maria_pm: thanks — customer is getting hit pretty hard, they reported 12% error rate over the last hour and said they might throttle traffic. We need an ETA for mitigations and a short customer note.

jordan_sre: immediate mitigation options: 1) scale up pool capacity (add more reserved GPUs) 2) force fallback to the previous model version (v2.3.7) for that customer route 3) temporarily cap batch size/disable dynamic batching for the customer's route. I'm running a canary scale up now.

alex.connor: tried rolling restart of the node pool and pinned a canary to v2.3.7 — crashes still happen on some nodes but frequency dropped. Repro pattern looks related to sequence length: long inputs (>2048 tokens) + batchsize>1 trigger repeatable crash within ~30–60s of processing the request. Repro curl (internal):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.host/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -d '{"model":"product-gen-v2.3.8","input":"'`python -c "print('x'*2500)"`'" ,"max_tokens":512}'
```

When I run that against a repro pod I see the same OOM/abort stack above.

emily_support: customer asked if this is related to the recent quantization changes. Any confirmation?

alex.connor: likely. The v2.3.8 change touched memory allocation paths for KV-cache with mixed precision; under long sequence workloads it increases peak allocation. I matched the crash to a single commit hash: `commit abcdef123456` (memory allocator tweak).

jordan_sre: can we get a kernel dmesg showing OOM killer? Alex, can you paste dmesg around kill time?

alex.connor: dmesg lines from the host where the crash occurred:

```
[Mar 15 08:12:34] Out of memory: Killed process 12453 (inference_worker) total-vm:12000000kB, anon-rss:9800000kB, file-rss:0kB, shmem-rss:0kB
[Mar 15 08:12:34] oom_reaper: reaped process 12453 (inference_worker), now anon-rss:0kB
```

So the kernel OOM killed the worker. That matches the runtime OOM.

maria_pm: ok, we need a short customer note: 1) root cause suspected, 2) immediate mitigation steps, 3) ETA.

jordan_sre: mitigation plan executed now: rollback route to model v2.3.7 (in progress), set customer route config to `batch_size:1` and `dynamic_batching: false` so each request runs single-shot, temporarily increase node pool by 20% while we investigate. Also adding an alert for worker restart rate > 5/min per node.

emily_support: did we capture core dump / heap profile? Customer asked for deep-dive.

alex.connor: need to enable core dumps on the failing node — steps I pushed to the node: `ulimit -c unlimited` and reconfigured systemd service with `LimitCORE=infinity`. Also added `--dump-heap-on-failure` to the worker binary. Asking infra for the archive location once it triggers.

ops-oncall-bot: deploy rollback of route big-ecom/product-gen -> v2.3.7 started by alex.connor at 08:29 UTC. Rollout status: 20% -> 100% (expected 2m).

alex.connor: after rollback + batching cap, error rate dropped from 12% -> 0.9% in last 10m. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/err-rate?route=big-ecom/product-gen (link internal). Putting a temporary rate-limit on customer to protect cluster while we root cause.

jordan_sre: long-term: revert that allocator commit and run mem-stress tests with long-sequence workloads in CI. Also add regression test that simulates 3x concurrent requests with sequence length 4k. I'll open a follow-up PR.

maria_pm: customer update drafted and sent: apology + rollback completed + temporary config changes + we are doing a deep-dive and will share a timeline. They asked for a root-cause and postmortem within 48h.

emily_support: thanks team. Can we capture the core dumps and run heap profiles off-hours? Also add an internal postmortem and include remediation (revert commit + test + alert).

alex.connor: confirmed core dump captured on one pod and uploaded to s3://redwood-dumps/C-4892/12453-core-20260315.tar.gz. Initial heap profile shows a large spike in device allocations just before OOM. I'll file a bug with the commit as cause: BUG-3372. Revert PR opened: PR#4521.

jordan_sre: closing this incident thread — mitigation in place, rollback validated, follow-up action items: BUG-3372, PR#4521 revert, add CI stress test, add restart-rate alert. :white_check_mark:

emily_support: customer notified and monitoring. Will update ticket and escalate billing questions to finance if needed. Thanks all.
